quote: Users increasingly rely on LLMs to discover, compare, and make product decisions through natural language interfaces.
The LLM is free to recommend any number of products in its preferred ordering. Retrieved rankings are then compared to control ones, in which no product is attacked.
LLM-based product recommendation has become an increasingly prevalent component of user-facing systems, with LLMs now integrated into search engines, conversational agents, and e-commerce platforms.
datasets: fictitious coffee machines, cameras and books
outputs: Generated product recommendation lists (ranked textual lists)
product recommendations in natural language in response to user queries such as "I'm looking for {product category}. Can you give me some suggestions?"

quote: Evaluation focuses on assessing how product recommendations change pre-and post-attack. To better capture these effects, we use two key metrics: • Recommendation rate (Rate) -how often a product is recommended... • Recommendation position (Pos)... We also include standard ranking metrics, such as Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR)...

We use two key metrics: Recommendation rate (Rate) – how often a product is recommended by the LLM, and Recommendation position (Pos) – the rank or order in which the product appears when it is recommended. We also include standard ranking metrics, such as Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR).
